notes: Check batch 6, skill condition, at 192abf3 with uncommitted changes to idiomatic-elixir/: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. skill_hash 40c558766911fda74c71db955ccb8d004adbc77cf83dc8e44539667cc9de12c1 in every result.json equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md and references/testing.md in all four and on references/processes.md in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not haiku-2, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (testing.md and processes.md) is met in 3 of 4. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changed rule (uncommitted): "Assert with patterns" (references/testing.md) gained the sentence that now decides its == verdicts: "Put the call under test on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right: a failure prints left and right in that order, and `assert [] == subscribers(server, "news")` reads backwards." 1 of 4 runs violate, sonnet-2, with the expected literal on the left three times: line 42: assert :ok == Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()); line 85: assert :ok == Subscriptions.publish(server, "news", %{headline: "Hello"}); line 121: assert :ok == Subscriptions.publish(server, "news", :update). These are the only assert ... == ... lines with a literal on the left in the four files. haiku-1 puts :ok on the right (line 42: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()) == :ok, also lines 47 and 56); haiku-2 and sonnet-1 assert :ok with a = pattern (e.g. haiku-2 line 41, sonnet-1 line 47), which the sentence does not govern; every subscribers/2 comparison in all four files has the call on the left (sonnet-2 included, e.g. line 48). The pin/whole-value sentence (unchanged since 0397dec) is broken by no run. Previous: 0 of 5 in 2026-10-22-b, 0 of 4 in check-4, under the text without this sentence.

Changed since 0397dec (committed at 192abf3, already graded in check-4): the test-name paragraph of "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour"; the verdict rests on "A name that only says the call did not fail (`"returns :ok"`, `"works"`, `"succeeds with an empty cart"`) tells the reader of a failure nothing; name the value and the condition (`"returns an error for an unknown coupon"`) or the effect (`"adds the item to the cart"`)." 2 of 4 runs violate, both Sonnet, both on test names: sonnet-1 line 134: test "succeeds for a topic without subscribers", %{server: server} do (the "succeeds ..." shape the sentence lists) and sonnet-2 line 41: test "returns :ok", %{server: server} do (the rule's own example). check-4 had 0 of 4, 2026-10-22-b 2 of 5. Borderline names graded clean to the check-4 standard: sonnet-2 line 120: test "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" (as check-4 and 2026-10-22-b graded "does nothing ..."), sonnet-2 line 143: test "survives publishing to the topic the process left" and sonnet-1 line 180: test "keeps the server running when the process crashes" (as check-4 graded "keeps the server running"). No describe block joins two functions; each run has one condition block "when a subscribed process exits" (haiku-1 and sonnet-2 with a named setup, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 with an inline setup), and sonnet-1 adds describe "start_link/1" for its missing-mailer test.

New rule in the index for this case: "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" (SKILL.md), deciding text "Right after `@moduledoc`, group each kind together, in that order". Directive order per run, in Notify.SubscriptionsTest: haiku-1 line 19 use ExUnit.Case, async: true / line 21 alias Notify.Subscriptions (use, alias); haiku-2 line 20 use ExUnit.Case, async: true / lines 22-23 alias Notify.Subscriptions, alias Notify.TestMailer, then line 25 @registry (use, alias, alias); sonnet-1 line 18 use ExUnit.Case, async: true / lines 20-21 alias Notify.Subscriptions, alias Notify.SubscriptionsTest.TestMailer (use, alias, alias); sonnet-2 line 23 use ExUnit.Case, async: true / lines 25-26 alias Notify.Subscriptions, alias Notify.SubscriptionsTest.TestMailer (use, alias, alias). No run writes import or require. The test modules have no @moduledoc and the directives open the module body; the TestMailer modules hold only @moduledoc false and @behaviour Notify.Mailer, no directives. 0 of 4 violate, graded clean; the prompt leaves little room to break it, since only use and alias are needed.

The other five graded rules are unchanged since 0397dec and graded to the 2026-10-22-b standard; all five are clean in 4 of 4 runs. All use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing TestMailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name; sonnet-1 (lines 36-41) asserts the missing-mailer failure with start_supervised/1 under a separate test-specific name and matches the KeyError reason; subscriber helpers are bare spawn/1 processes (graded clean as before); every exit wait monitors and asserts the :DOWN; refutes follow a synchronous call or a later assert_receive from the same sender; no Process.register, Application env, start_link call or elem/2. Process.sleep(:infinity) at sonnet-1 line 143 and sonnet-2 line 151 is the body that keeps a subscriber alive, not a wait for work, and is not counted (as in previous sweeps); sonnet-1 line 186: assert Process.alive?(server) is one assertion after a :DOWN wait, not polling.

SKILL.md rules changed since 192abf3 outside this case's list (the defstruct sentence in "Update structs with `%{struct | field: value}`" and the new "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call"): no file has a defstruct; haiku-1 lines 32-37 return a setup map whose server: value is a start_supervised!(...) call that mix format wrapped, but the map is a return value, not a call argument, and the call's own argument is a one-line tuple, so it is not counted. other_violations is empty in all four runs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings (haiku-1 12 tests, haiku-2 11, sonnet-1 17, sonnet-2 15). All four pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json.
